# Composio toolkit research: 100 apps

> An agent researched 100 apps for Composio toolkit feasibility (auth, self-serve vs gated access, API surface, MCP,
> buildability) with a verbatim evidence quote behind every answer, then verified itself in 3 automated loops + a human sample.

Human accuracy check: pending.

## Machine-readable files
- [results.json](https://karanlokhande29.github.io/composio-toolkit-research/results.json): one object per app (schema: auth, access, api_surface, mcp, buildability, evidence, pass1, verification)
- [patterns.json](https://karanlokhande29.github.io/composio-toolkit-research/patterns.json): every aggregate number and the headline sentences
- [metrics.json](https://karanlokhande29.github.io/composio-toolkit-research/metrics.json): coverage, per-loop verification stats, accuracy
- [Source repo](https://github.com/karanLokhande29/composio-toolkit-research): README explains how to run the agent

## Headlines
- Static keys/tokens are the most common auth: 77 of 100 apps accept an API key or token, 74 support OAuth2, and 56 offer both - so most toolkits can start on API-key auth and add OAuth for multi-tenant use.
- Getting credentials is mostly self-serve: 74% of apps let a developer get working credentials alone (free or trial); 19 are gated by an admin, app review, partner programme or sales.
- Gating clusters by category: Developer, Infra and Data platforms is the most self-serve (100%), Marketing, Ads, Email and Social the least (40%).
- The most common blocker is 'paid plan' (13 apps); 58 apps are ready today, 36 ready with caveats, 6 blocked.
- MCP is already mainstream: 50 vendors ship an official MCP server and 25 more have only community servers.
- Composio already has toolkits for 80 of the 100; 4 self-serve, ready apps have no Composio toolkit yet - the cheapest net-new wins.
